title: One or two omitted winters can reverse basin-volume forecast gains in a 2000-2024 ENSO score audit
abstract: We audited the sign of added warm-water volume forecast scores for 25 winters in 2000-2024. Separate February and August linear fits used earlier annual targets, current Nino 3.4 temperature and its three-month change. Adding basin volume gave mean squared error gains of 0.11089 and 0.01348 C squared. Both conditional three-year block intervals included zero. Exact bounds over omitted test winters show that all single omissions retain the February gain, but 14 of 300 pair omissions reverse it. Two of 25 single omissions reverse the August gain. Absolute-error gains need three and two omissions to reverse their signs. Fixed training changes these results. This is an exploratory score influence audit with revised NOAA products. Omitted test years remain in later training. The counts are finite-sample properties, not probabilities of future skill or reasons to remove extreme events. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and two figures are included. External records can be regenerated separately.
